item.title: Rams-Jaguars could be trade partners before Tuesday’s deadline
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Braden Fiske #55 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the first half of a game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams might have to part ways with an important piece of their defensive line to acquire the wide receiver help they desperately need before the NFL trade deadline. Braden Fiske could become the trade asset that makes a potential deal possible, particularly if the Jacksonville Jaguars are willing to discuss Brian Thomas Jr. A Fiske-for-Thomas swap could make sense for both organizations. Jacksonville recently lost defensive tackle Davon Hamilton for the season after he tore his quadriceps, creating an immediate need for additional help along the interior defensive line. Fiske could provide the Jaguars with a young, disruptive defensive lineman who still has plenty of upside and multiple years of team control. James Gladstone, the Jaguars GM, was a big proponent of the Braden Fiske pick in 2024. Could he want to reunite with the 2nd rounder with shipping away Brian Thomas Jr to the Rams? Gladstone here gushing about Braden Fiske before the #Rams traded up to get him 👀 #Jaguars https://t.co/bgrflySjRY — @UCjags (@UCJags) November 9, 2026 Meanwhile, the Rams have a different problem to solve. Their offense continues to funnel opportunities through Puka Nacua, while the supporting cast has struggled to consistently separate and make plays. Adding Thomas would give Matthew Stafford another legitimate outside receiving threat and provide Sean McVay with a much-needed offensive weapon. There is also a potential roster squeeze in Los Angeles. Kobie Turner is working his way back from a groin injury, and his return figures to eat into Fiske’s playing time along the defensive front. That doesn’t necessarily make Fiske expendable, but it could make him a more attractive trade chip. Sacrificing a promising defensive lineman is never an easy decision. However, if the Rams can turn Fiske into a young receiver like Thomas, it might be a worthwhile investment in their championship aspirations.

item.title: GametimeCT Top 10 Football Poll, Week 10 (Nov. 9): First place votes split, St. Joesph is new No. 1
item.description: St. Joseph's player celebrate defeating New Canaan in the CIAC football game between No. 2 St. Joseph and No. 3 New Canaan high schools. Friday November 6, 2026, New Canaan High School, New Canaan, Conn. (H John Voorhees III/Hearst Connecticut Media) For the second straight week, there is a new No. 1 team in Connecticut high school football . A week after Fairfield Ludlowe took over the top spot for dethroning New Canaan, St. Joseph has now taken over as No. 1 after handing New Canaan its second consecutive loss. The Hogs defeated New Canaan 21-14 on Friday, while Fairfield Ludlowe had won 34-31 the week prior. Both St. Joseph and Ludlowe received 11 first-place votes, but in the end it was St. Joseph that came out in front with 638 points in the vote against Ludlowe's 636. While St. Joseph received 11 second-place votes, the difference was that Ludlowe received 10 second-place votes and one third-place vote (Hand received the second-place vote on that ballot). This is the first time since the end of the 2019 season that St. Joseph is Connecticut's top team. New London, now on the outside looking in, received 288 points. New Canaan, which suffered its second straight loss, fell from No. 3 to No. 4 while Hand moved up from No. 5 to No. 3. item.title: Falcons say goodbye to former Bengals DB Jessie Bates III
item.description: Atlanta Falcons defensive back Jessie Bates III was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars one day after the team's NFL Week 9 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. The Falcons thanked Bates with a tweet , "for everything on and off the field." The Bengals' second-round pick in the 2018 NFL Draft faced his former team for the first time since leaving Cincinnati for Atlanta after the 2022 season. Bates led the Falcons with 14 tackles against the Bengals, including 11 solo tackles. Bengals head coach Zac Taylor shared praise of Bates earlier in the week. "I feel like I've just seen him a lot on TV, on tape, and I think we all love Jessie," Taylor told reporters Nov. 2 . "Everybody feels the same way about Jessie here. And (I've) always been pulling for him and really happy to see him be successful, a Pro Bowler (in 2023), like he's earned all that and (is a) really easy guy to root for." Taylor coached Bates for four seasons. Bates played in 79 games over five seasons with the Bengals. He has played in 59 games over four seasons in Atlanta. Bates entered the game with one interception through eight games this season. He's returned an interception for a touchdown in each of the past three seasons. item.description: Maxx Crosby is making his position on the NFL trade deadline clear. Despite renewed speculation about his future with the Las Vegas Raiders following Sunday’s loss to the San Francisco 49ers, the star defensive end expects to remain with the organization. Maxx Crosby on trade deadline: I expect to play for the Raiders. https://t.co/d4x6WoSrnz — ProFootballTalk (@ProFootballTalk) November 9, 2026 With the trade deadline approaching Tuesday, Crosby delivered a blunt response when asked about the possibility of being moved, reiterating his commitment to the Raiders. item.title: Is there an alternative to DLS? Exploring various methods to calculate scores in rain-affected matches
item.description: Is there an alternative to DLS? Exploring various methods to calculate scores in rain-affected matches originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: DLS calculates targets using resources, meaning overs remaining and wickets in hand together. The VJD method is the only serious modern rival, and it is used in Indian domestic cricket. Earlier systems failed because they ignored wickets, most notoriously at the 1992 World Cup. What is the DLS method? The Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method is the system cricket uses to reset a target when rain or any other interruption shortens a limited-overs match. It was devised by two English statisticians, Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis, introduced in 1997 and adopted by the ICC two years later. Its central idea is that a batting side has two resources at any moment, overs remaining and wickets in hand, and that both have to be counted. A team 120 for 0 after 25 overs is in a far stronger position than one 120 for 9 after the same 25, and any fair method has to say so. DLS assigns every combination of overs and wickets a percentage of total resources, then adjusts the target in proportion to how much each side actually had. The method was renamed in November 2014, when Australian statistician Steven Stern took over as custodian and revised the model to reflect higher modern scoring rates, particularly in T20. It exists in two forms. The Standard Edition works from a printed table and can be applied with a calculator, which is what club and lower-level cricket use. The Professional Edition runs on software and is the version used in international cricket. MORE: What is the DLS method? Duckworth–Lewis rules explained for ODIs and T20Is What are the alternatives to the DLS method? Several systems have been used or proposed; some of them are predecessors, one cricket-abandoned, and one a genuine modern rival. Average Run Rate The oldest approach, used from the early days of one-day cricket until 1991. Team 2's target was simply Team 1's run rate multiplied by the reduced number of overs, so the chasing side only had to match the rate. Its flaw was that it ignored wickets entirely. A side nine down with a healthy run rate was treated identically to one that had lost nothing, which meant the method systematically favoured the team batting second. Every over removed was an over they no longer had to survive. Australia pushed hardest for its replacement, with Allan Border among those criticising it publicly after a defeat where a West Indies target was cut in a way that lowered their required rate rather than raising it. item.title: Man Utd yet to make decision on Carrick's future
item.description: Michael Carrick has won 15 out of 32 games since taking over from Ruben Amorim as Manchester United's head coach in January [Getty Images] Manchester United's board is yet to make a final decision on Michael Carrick's future. The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday means United, who are 18th in the table, have made their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years. The draw was Carrick's third match in charge since the board decided to give the 45-year-old more time to improve the side's form after a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October. The board felt Carrick - and the players - had earned the opportunity to show that they could turn the club's fortunes around, while the heirachy were also aware that November's two-week break would offer an opportunity to reassess the situation in a calmer manner. They are determined to do exactly that, knowing the results - one win, one draw and one defeat - and performances United have delivered in the past three games offer a mixed view of Carrick's tenure. Conceding eight goals, winning only once and dropping into the relegation zone are obvious negatives. However, it is also felt fighting back from two goals down three times over the past two games showed that the players remain behind Carrick. United's heirachy explored the possibility of replacing Carrick after the loss to Bournemouth last month, with ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann considered. Carrick said after the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa that he would not step down, but chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will be influential in the decision whether to keep the former Middlesbrough boss. United travel to arch rivals Liverpool on 22 November in their first match after the international break, with Carrick's side in 18th place in the Premier League. With just one league win so far this term, it is United's lowest position having played 10 matches since the 1986-87 campaign. Following the Anfield trip, five of United's next seven league opponents are in the bottom half of the league. This includes the four other sides currently in the bottom five, with meetings against Coventry, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, all at Old Trafford. Whether Carrick keeps his job or not, United will continue to struggle unless they stop conceding goals with such regularity. Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich have let in more than United's 19 league goals. They have conceded 15 times in the past three matches in all competitions. Their only clean sheet this term came against Azerbaijan title winners Sabah FK in the Champions League. item.title: Former Real Madrid manager heaps praise on Arda Guler: ‘Always in the right place, where he needs to be’
item.description: Former Real Madrid manager heaps praise on Arda Guler: ‘Always in the right place, where he needs to be’ Real Madrid’s exceptional comeback after the international break of the season deserves more recognition, with the team currently on a run of eight consecutive victories in all competitions. A key catalyst for Real Madrid’s success in recent weeks has been the performances of Arda Guler, who appears to have established himself as a first-team regular. Guler has been the creative spark Real Madrid needed in the final third and his combination play with Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe has caused havoc in opposition defences. Jorge Valdano sings praises of Guler In light of his recent performances, Guler has received unconditional praise from former Real Madrid manager and director Jorge Valdano. Guler is on sensational form right now. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) “Guler is wonderful. He is always in the right place, where he needs to be. Playing out wide and having an extraordinary influence on Real Madrid’s game. He is playing with great confidence,” he said (h/t Defensa Central ). Valdano’s comments come on the back of Guler’s brilliant performance against Valencia, with the Turkish international chipping in with a goal and an assist in a 3-0 victory for Los Blancos . “He has extraordinary vision, decision-making and ball control,” he added. Guler could soon be rewarded for his performances, with the Real Madrid star reportedly signing a contract extension that is yet to be officiated. Valdano on Real Madrid’s form Valdano went on to talk about Real Madrid’s form and the La Liga title race, admitting that the team is looking stronger with each passing game. Valdano is confident about this Real Madrid team. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) “Madrid are becoming increasingly solid and convincing. They emerge stronger from this matchday, despite Barcelona’s victory at the Metropolitano,” Valdano said. The former Real Madrid CEO also offered his thoughts on the game against Valencia, adding that the referee’s decision to show Jose Gaya a red card for his dangerous tackle on Kylian Mbappe was the right one. “I have no doubts that Gaya’s dismissal was justified. It was a red card because he never went for the ball. He didn’t touch it either. Had he done so, the decision would have been debatable and he would have had a case in his defence,” he said. Real Madrid are heading into the international break with a three point deficit to leaders Barcelona and thanks to Atletico Madrid’s defeat, they have climbed to second place in the standings.

item.description: Chiefs get even more banged up but avoid “the big one.” Patrick Mahomes ’ arm was dangling by his side. Then, as he so often does, he went “LeBron mode.” It would be difficult to count the number of times I have seen LeBron James suffer what appears to be certain calamity only for the 21st century’s basketball GOAT to walk it off. The same has become true of Mahomes, who though he has missed time, never seems to land on the shelf when it counts . It counts more than ever for a Chiefs team that can’t waste another season after last year’s fiasco and subsequent “big one,” a torn ACL, for Mahomes. The big one is not back for 2026, but all the other questions remain. Namely: Who can Mahomes actually throw to? The answer for Week 10 is “not Xavier Worthy ” after the star-crossed receiver suffered what appeared to be a multi-week hamstring injury against the Jets. This is now the second or third time this season the Chiefs' offense has suffered a loss it cannot afford. Not because Worthy has been so good or productive, but because the “next man up” will somehow be even worse. The Chiefs are dipping into depth they do not have. That’s why one of the greatest players we have ever seen will remain affixed to the QB1/2 borderline for the foreseeable future — unless a trade deadline addition or two changes things. Five Week 9 Storylines Puka Nacua injures his knee and the Rams hold their breath. Sean McVay is a football genius, but his 2026 plan is pretty simple: Get the ball to Nacua as many times as humanly possible. This is a risky approach with any player, but especially one with Nacua’s injury history and pre-existing 2026 ailments. No matter, the Super Bowl favorites’ season went sideways to begin the year and the team is now mired in comeback mode. Things could get so, so much worse if Nacua’s Monday MRI turns up a multi-week issue, but multi-month at least appears to be off the table. Of course, even a few weeks on the shelf would be enough to cost many fantasy managers their playoff spots. That’s extra true since no Rams help is coming via the waiver wire. There’s really only one thing you can do: Join the Rams in waiting to exhale. Justin Herbert’s season manages to get even more miserable. Having what is probably the worst season of the decade by any established “franchise player,” Herbert now has a new bone break to deal with: Same as the old break . Yes, Herbie seems to have again fractured a bone on his non-throwing hand. He played through it in 2025, but in 2026 this team is 0-8. OC Mike McDaniel’s gig has weeks to live. Head coach Jim Harbaugh’s job might be down to months. Perhaps they will be able to convince Herbert to push through his injury, but then again, do they even want him to at this point? item.title: Tom Brady Stunned to Learn He Was Babysat by Packers Player’s Mom: ‘Hope I Was Good’
item.description: Tom Brady and Evan Williams Credit: Brace Hemmelgarn/Getty; Todd Rosenberg/Getty NEED TO KNOW Tom Brady was “shocked” to learn current Green Bay Packers safety Evan Williams’ mom Dani Williams used to babysit him as a child Brady, 49, and Williams, 25, both grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area “I hope I was good!” the seven-time Super Bowl champion joked about his child self Tom Brady got a blast from the past on Sunday afternoon when he found out the mom of current Green Bay Packers safety Evan Williams used to babysit him when he was a kid. “I don’t get shocked very often, but I was shocked,” Brady, 49, told his Fox Sports broadcast partner Kevin Burkhardt as they recounted the story during the Sunday, Nov. 8 game between the Packers and Brady’s former New England Patriots. “Evan Williams grew up in the Bay Area, and his mom babysat me when I was five. I told her, ‘I hope I was good!’ ” Brady said with a laugh. “Maybe we should throw in an extra tip now for me being a bad boy.” The seven-time Super Bowl champion-turned-broadcaster told Burkhardt he met Williams, 25, prior to Sunday’s game in New England. As the two were talking about their shared hometown, Williams told Brady about their unique connection. Evan Williams Credit: Cooper Neill/Getty “He went to St. Francis High School, which is an awesome football school in the Bay Area, and I went to Serra High School, that’s now an awesome football school,” Brady explained during the broadcast. “And I said, ‘Evan, hey, St. Francis, you know, how was your record against Serra?’ He said, ‘Hey, I got a story for you! My mom used to babysit you!’ And I was like, ‘Man, I’m never surprised. What do you mean?’ ” While Brady told the story, Fox simultaneously showed Williams’ mom, Dani Williams, cheering on her son in the stands. And she had plenty to cheer about, as her son racked up four tackles and an interception during the Packers’ 45-27 rout of the Patriots.
